proves.claim: a landing run that throws ends with a failed step and done, with no owner.

land.jobs.throw-ends-done.why: A throwing run left an owner on a never-finishing job.

proves.claim: a landing run that stalls ends with a failed step and done, with no owner.

land.jobs.stall-ends-done.why: A stalled run must free its job rather than hold it forever.

proves.claim: a finish sequence stopped by LAND_PROOF_NOT_GREEN ends with a failed step and done, and stays so when resumed.

land.jobs.proof-not-green-stays-done.why: A refused proof must not be retried into a landing by a resume.

proves.claim: landing jobs are named by what they land, so a repeat finds the same row.

land.runs.job-named-by-landing.why: Names that vary per attempt would record one landing twice.

proves.claim: a hand landing runs the caller's check, record and publish around the one merge it answers, and pins the tooling.

land.runs.hand-landing-one-merge.why: The hand path must follow the same finish sequence as the lander.

proves.claim: a second hand landing of the same items and commit answers the same commit and records nothing again.
a hand landing killed in its record resumes from the saved steps, and a refusing check writes nothing.

land.runs.hand-landing-resumes.why: A killed landing must resume without redoing or half-recording.

proves.claim: a hand landing refuses no items, a short commit id, a missing record step and a lease held by another driver.

land.runs.hand-landing-refusals.why: Bad input must refuse before any step runs.

proves.claim: a batch landing records only a landed batch with a full tip, once, and answers the batch's own tip.

land.runs.batch-landing-once.why: A batch must never be recorded partial or twice.

proves.claim: the finish steps are six, in order, and the next one is read from what the log holds.

land.sequence.six-steps-in-order.why: The order is the contract resumes depend on.

proves.claim: a landing runs all six steps in order, each handed what the earlier ones wrote, and ends done with its lease released.

land.sequence.runs-all-steps.why: Each step needs the earlier steps' output, and the lease must not leak.

proves.claim: a finished landing runs nothing again, and a resumed one skips every step its log holds.

land.sequence.finished-and-resumed.why: Resuming must be safe to repeat.

proves.claim: a green receipt at exactly the composition's trees is reused and prove does not run; any other receipt is not.

land.sequence.reuses-exact-receipt.why: Reuse only a receipt that proved these exact trees.

proves.claim: a red or infra proof stops the landing before merge, and a later run stays stopped.
a landing whose live lease another driver holds is left alone, and it continues once the lease lapsed.

land.sequence.live-lease-respected.why: Two drivers must not land the same items at once.

proves.claim: the sequence refuses a missing owner, repo, job or step handler, and a step that answers the wrong shape.

land.sequence.refuses-bad-wiring.why: A mis-wired sequence must fail loudly before landing.

proves.claim: every land-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

land.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: every land test file that reads files opens with an input header naming the cells it reads.

land.inputs.declared.why: Affected-test selection can only see a reader that declares what it reads.

proves.claim: every land test header names cells or files by path and none declares the whole source tree.

land.inputs.rule-clean.why: A header naming nothing, or the whole tree, would hide a reader or defeat narrow selection.
